text: In Deutschland dürfen Menschen offen etwas gegen die Regierung sagen, weil …

en.text: In Germany, people are allowed to say something openly against the government because …
options: people have the right to vote.
en.context: Freedom of expression (Article 5 of the Basic Law) lets anyone voice criticism of those in power without fear of punishment. Being able to contradict the government is exactly what separates a democracy from a dictatorship.

text: In Deutschland können Eltern bis zum 14. Lebensjahr ihres Kindes entscheiden, ob es in der Schule am …

en.text: In Germany, parents can decide until their child is 14 whether it takes part at school in …
en.context: Religious education is the only school subject the Basic Law singles out: under Article 7, parents decide whether their child takes part, and from 14 the child decides for itself.

text: Deutschland ist ein Rechtsstaat. Was ist damit gemeint?
options: Alle Einwohnerinnen/Einwohner und der Staat müssen sich an die Gesetze halten.
Der Staat muss sich nicht an die Gesetze halten.
Nur Deutsche müssen die Gesetze befolgen.

en.text: Germany is a state governed by the rule of law. What does that mean?
options: All residents and the state itself must obey the law.
The state does not have to obey the law.
Only Germans have to follow the law.
en.context: In a Rechtsstaat the law binds everyone, the state included. Officials, police and ministers are as subject to the law as any resident, and courts can be asked to enforce that.

text: Welches Recht gehört zu den Grundrechten in Deutschland?

en.text: Which right is one of the basic rights in Germany?
options: taking the law into your own hands
en.context: Freedom of expression is one of the basic rights in Articles 1 to 19 of the Basic Law. Owning weapons or settling scores yourself are not rights at all.

text: Wahlen in Deutschland sind frei. Was bedeutet das?
options: Man darf Geld annehmen, wenn man dafür eine bestimmte Kandidatin/einen bestimmten Kandidaten wählt.
Nur Personen, die noch nie im Gefängnis waren, dürfen wählen.
Die Wählerin/der Wähler darf bei der Wahl weder beeinflusst noch zu einer bestimmten Stimmabgabe gezwungen werden und keine Nachteile durch die Wahl haben.

en.text: Elections in Germany are free. What does that mean?
options: You may accept money for voting for a particular candidate.
Only people who have never been in prison are allowed to vote.
Voters may be neither influenced nor forced to cast a particular vote, and must suffer no disadvantage from voting.
Everyone entitled to vote must vote.
en.context: Free means nobody may pressure, bribe or coerce you over your vote, and you may not be penalised for how you voted. It does not mean voting is compulsory, nor does a criminal record generally remove the right to vote.

text: Wie heißt die deutsche Verfassung?

en.text: What is the German constitution called?
en.context: The German constitution is called the Grundgesetz, or Basic Law. The name was chosen in 1949 as a deliberately provisional one, because the founders hoped for a joint constitution once Germany was reunited.

text: Welches Recht gehört zu den Grundrechten, die nach der deutschen Verfassung garantiert werden? Das Recht auf …

en.text: Which right is one of the basic rights guaranteed by the German constitution? The right to …
en.context: Freedom of faith and conscience is guaranteed by Article 4. Entertainment, work and housing are things the state may support, but they are not basic rights you can claim in court.

text: Was steht nicht im Grundgesetz von Deutschland?
options: Die Würde des Menschen ist unantastbar.
Alle sollen gleich viel Geld haben.
Jeder Mensch darf seine Meinung sagen.
Alle sind vor dem Gesetz gleich.

en.text: What is not in Germany's Basic Law?
options: Everyone should have the same amount of money.
Everyone is equal before the law.
en.context: The Basic Law guarantees dignity, free expression and equality before the law, but it never promises equal wealth. It sets the rules of the game, not the outcome.

text: Welches Grundrecht gilt in Deutschland nur für Ausländerinnen/Ausländer? Das Grundrecht auf …

en.text: Which basic right applies in Germany only to foreign nationals? The basic right to …
en.context: The right to asylum in Article 16a applies only to people who are not German citizens, which makes it the one basic right reserved for foreign nationals. Dignity and free expression apply to everybody.

text: Was ist mit dem deutschen Grundgesetz vereinbar?

en.text: What is compatible with Germany's Basic Law?
en.context: A fine is an ordinary criminal penalty and entirely compatible with the Basic Law. Corporal punishment, torture and the death penalty are all forbidden; Article 102 abolished capital punishment outright.

text: Wie wird die Verfassung der Bundesrepublik Deutschland genannt?

en.text: What is the constitution of the Federal Republic of Germany called?
en.context: It is the Grundgesetz, the Basic Law. It came into force on 23 May 1949 and, after reunification, became the constitution for the whole of Germany.

text: Eine Partei im Deutschen Bundestag will die Pressefreiheit abschaffen. Ist das möglich?
options: Ja, wenn mehr als die Hälfte der Abgeordneten im Bundestag dafür sind.
Ja, aber dazu müssen zwei Drittel der Abgeordneten im Bundestag dafür sein.
Nein, denn die Pressefreiheit ist ein Grundrecht. Sie kann nicht abgeschafft werden.
Nein, denn nur der Bundesrat kann die Pressefreiheit abschaffen.

en.text: A party in the German Bundestag wants to abolish freedom of the press. Is that possible?
options: Yes, if more than half of the members of the Bundestag are in favour.
Yes, but two thirds of the members of the Bundestag must be in favour.
No, because freedom of the press is a basic right. It cannot be abolished.
No, because only the Bundesrat can abolish freedom of the press.
en.context: Freedom of the press is part of the basic rights, and Article 79(3) puts the core of those rights beyond the reach of any majority. Not even a unanimous Bundestag could abolish it.

text: Im Parlament steht der Begriff "Opposition" für …
options: die Fraktion mit den meisten Abgeordneten.
alle Parteien, die bei der letzten Wahl die 5%-Hürde erreichen konnten.
alle Abgeordneten, die nicht zu der Regierungspartei/den Regierungsparteien gehören.

en.text: In parliament, the term "opposition" stands for …
options: the parliamentary group with the most members.
all parties that cleared the 5% threshold at the last election.
all members who do not belong to the governing party or parties.
en.context: The opposition is made up of all members who do not belong to the governing party or parties. Its job is to scrutinise the government and offer an alternative.

text: Meinungsfreiheit in Deutschland heißt, dass ich …
options: Passanten auf der Straße beschimpfen darf.
meine Meinung im Internet äußern kann.
Nazi-, Hamas- oder Islamischer Staat-Symbole öffentlich tragen darf.
meine Meinung nur dann äußern darf, solange ich der Regierung nicht widerspreche.

en.text: Freedom of expression in Germany means that I …
options: may insult passers-by in the street.
can express my opinion on the internet.
may display Nazi, Hamas or Islamic State symbols in public.
may only express my opinion as long as I do not contradict the government.
en.context: Freedom of expression covers stating your opinion in public, including online. It does not protect insulting people or displaying the symbols of banned organisations.

text: Was verbietet das deutsche Grundgesetz?

en.text: What does Germany's Basic Law prohibit?
en.context: Article 12 of the Basic Law forbids forced labour. Choosing your occupation freely and working abroad are precisely the freedoms it protects.

text: Wann ist die Meinungsfreiheit in Deutschland eingeschränkt?
options: bei der öffentlichen Verbreitung falscher Behauptungen über einzelne Personen

en.text: When is freedom of expression restricted in Germany?
options: when false claims about individuals are spread in public
when opinions are expressed about the federal government
en.context: Free expression ends where it damages other people's rights, for example by spreading untrue factual claims about them. Criticising the government, the state or religion is fully protected.

text: Die deutschen Gesetze verbieten …
options: Ungleichbehandlung der Bürgerinnen und Bürger durch den Staat.

en.text: German law prohibits …
options: unequal treatment of citizens by the state.
en.context: Article 3 obliges the state to treat people equally, so unequal treatment by the state is what the law forbids. Expression, petitions and assembly are rights the law guarantees, not bans.

text: Welches Grundrecht ist in Artikel 1 des Grundgesetzes der Bundesrepublik Deutschland garantiert?

en.text: Which basic right is guaranteed in Article 1 of the Basic Law of the Federal Republic of Germany?
en.context: Article 1 opens with the sentence "Human dignity shall be inviolable." It is placed first deliberately, as the foundation on which every other basic right rests.

text: Was versteht man unter dem Recht der "Freizügigkeit" in Deutschland?
options: Man darf sich seinen Wohnort selbst aussuchen.
Man darf sich für eine andere Religion entscheiden.
Man darf sich in der Öffentlichkeit nur leicht bekleidet bewegen.

en.text: What is meant by the right of "freedom of movement" in Germany?
options: You may choose where you live.
You may decide to follow a different religion.
You may go about in public only lightly dressed.
en.context: Freizügigkeit is the right to move to and settle anywhere in Germany. It is about choosing where you live, not about what you wear or which job you take.

text: Eine Partei in Deutschland verfolgt das Ziel, eine Diktatur zu errichten. Sie ist dann …

en.text: A party in Germany pursues the aim of establishing a dictatorship. It is then …
options: committed to the rule of law.
en.context: A party aiming to set up a dictatorship works against the free democratic basic order and is therefore unconstitutional. Only the Federal Constitutional Court may ban a party on those grounds.

text: Welches ist das Wappen der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?

en.text: Which is the coat of arms of the Federal Republic of Germany?
en.context: The federal coat of arms is the black eagle on a golden shield. It has been in use since 1950 and goes back to the Weimar Republic's design.

text: Was für eine Staatsform hat Deutschland?

en.text: What form of state does Germany have?
en.context: Germany is a republic: its head of state is elected, not born into the office. Republic, democracy, federal state and welfare state are all described in Article 20.

text: In Deutschland sind die meisten Erwerbstätigen …
options: selbstständig mit einer eigenen Firma tätig.
bei einer Firma oder Behörde beschäftigt.

en.text: In Germany, most working people are …
options: working voluntarily for a federal state.
self-employed with a company of their own.
employed by a company or a public authority.
en.context: Most working people in Germany are employees of a company or a public authority rather than self-employed. Roughly nine in ten workers are in dependent employment.

text: Wie viele Bundesländer hat die Bundesrepublik Deutschland?

en.text: How many federal states does the Federal Republic of Germany have?
en.context: Germany has 16 federal states. There were 11 in the West until 1990, when five eastern states joined and Berlin was reunited.

text: Was ist kein Bundesland der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?

en.text: Which is not a federal state of the Federal Republic of Germany?
en.context: Alsace-Lorraine is a region of France, not a German federal state. The other three are all part of the 16.

text: Deutschland ist …

en.text: Germany is …
options: a democratic and social federal state.
a social and socialist federal state.
en.context: Article 20 describes Germany as a democratic and social federal state. Democratic because power comes from the people, social because the state provides for those in need.

text: Deutschland ist …

en.text: Germany is …
en.context: Germany is a federal state: power is shared between the federation and the 16 states, each with its own parliament and government.

text: Wer wählt in Deutschland die Abgeordneten zum Bundestag?

en.text: Who elects the members of the Bundestag in Germany?
en.context: The members of the Bundestag are elected by the people entitled to vote. All state authority emanates from the people, and elections are how that happens.

text: Welches Tier ist das Wappentier der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?

en.text: Which animal is the heraldic animal of the Federal Republic of Germany?
en.context: The heraldic animal is the eagle. The Bundesadler appears on the coat of arms, on coins and in the plenary chamber of the Bundestag.

text: Was ist kein Merkmal unserer Demokratie?

en.text: What is not a feature of our democracy?
en.context: Press censorship is the opposite of democracy; Article 5 states plainly that censorship shall not take place. Regular elections, free expression and several parties are all essential features.

text: Die Zusammenarbeit von Parteien zur Bildung einer Regierung nennt man in Deutschland …

en.text: In Germany, parties working together to form a government is called a …
en.context: When parties work together to form a government, that is a coalition. German governments are usually coalitions, because one party rarely wins a majority on its own.

text: Was ist keine staatliche Gewalt in Deutschland?

en.text: What is not a branch of state power in Germany?
en.context: The press is not a branch of state power. The three branches are the legislature, the executive and the judiciary; the press is often called the "fourth estate", but it is private and independent of the state.

text: Welche Aussage ist richtig? In Deutschland …
options: sind Staat und Religionsgemeinschaften voneinander getrennt.
ist der Staat abhängig von den Religionsgemeinschaften.
bilden Staat und Religionsgemeinschaften eine Einheit.

en.text: Which statement is correct? In Germany …
options: the state and religious communities are separate from one another.
the religious communities form the state.
the state depends on the religious communities.
the state and religious communities form a single unit.
en.context: In Germany the state and religious communities are separate. There is no state church, though churches do cooperate with the state in areas such as schools and welfare.

text: Was ist Deutschland nicht?

en.text: What is Germany not?
options: a state governed by the rule of law
en.context: Germany is not a monarchy. It is a democracy, a state governed by the rule of law and a welfare state, all at once.

text: Womit finanziert der deutsche Staat die Sozialversicherung?

en.text: How does the German state finance social insurance?
en.context: Social insurance is financed by contributions (Sozialabgaben) that employers and employees pay from wages. Church tax and donations fund quite different things.

text: Welche Maßnahme schafft in Deutschland soziale Sicherheit?

en.text: Which measure creates social security in Germany?
en.context: Health insurance is one of the five branches of statutory social insurance and is what protects people financially when they fall ill. Car and buildings insurance are private cover for property.

text: Wie werden die Regierungschefinnen/Regierungschefs der meisten Bundesländer in Deutschland genannt?

en.text: What are the heads of government of most federal states in Germany called?
en.context: In most federal states the head of government is called Ministerpräsident. The three city states are the exception: Berlin has a Governing Mayor, Hamburg and Bremen a First Mayor and a President of the Senate.

text: Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland ist ein demokratischer und sozialer …

en.text: The Federal Republic of Germany is a democratic and social …
en.context: Article 20 describes the Federal Republic as a democratic and social federal state. A confederation would be a looser association of independent states.

text: Was hat jedes deutsche Bundesland?

en.text: What does every German federal state have?
en.context: Every federal state has its own government, its own parliament and its own constitution. None has its own army, currency or foreign minister.

text: Mit welchen Worten beginnt die deutsche Nationalhymne?

en.text: With which words does the German national anthem begin?
options: Völker, hört die Signale … (Peoples, hear the signals …)
Einigkeit und Recht und Freiheit … (Unity and justice and freedom …)
Freude schöner Götterfunken … (Joy, beautiful spark of the gods …)
en.context: The anthem is the third verse of the Deutschlandlied, beginning "Einigkeit und Recht und Freiheit" — unity and justice and freedom. Only that third verse is the national anthem.

text: Warum gibt es in einer Demokratie mehr als eine Partei?
options: weil dadurch die unterschiedlichen Meinungen der Bürgerinnen und Bürger vertreten werden
damit Bestechung in der Politik begrenzt wird

en.text: Why is there more than one party in a democracy?
options: because this is how the differing opinions of citizens are represented
so that bribery in politics is kept in check
en.context: Several parties exist so that the different opinions among citizens can actually be represented. A single-party state cannot offer voters a genuine choice.

text: Wer beschließt in Deutschland ein neues Gesetz?

en.text: Who passes a new law in Germany?
en.context: Laws are passed by parliament — the Bundestag, with the Bundesrat taking part where the states are affected. The government may propose bills, but it cannot enact them.

text: Wann kann in Deutschland eine Partei verboten werden?
options: wenn ihr Wahlkampf zu teuer ist
wenn sie gegen die Verfassung kämpft
wenn sie Kritik am Staatsoberhaupt äußert
wenn ihr Programm eine neue Richtung vorschlägt

en.text: When can a party be banned in Germany?
options: if its election campaign is too expensive
if it fights against the constitution
if it voices criticism of the head of state
if its programme proposes a new direction
en.context: A party may be banned only if it fights against the constitution, and only the Federal Constitutional Court can order it. Expensive campaigns or unpopular ideas are no grounds at all.

text: Wen kann man als Bürgerin/Bürger in Deutschland nicht direkt wählen?

en.text: Whom can citizens in Germany not elect directly?
en.context: The Federal President is elected by the Federal Convention, not by the people. Members of the Bundestag, state parliaments and the European Parliament are all elected directly.

text: Zu welcher Versicherung gehört die Pflegeversicherung?

en.text: Which type of insurance does long-term care insurance belong to?
en.context: Long-term care insurance is one of the five branches of statutory social insurance, alongside health, pension, unemployment and accident insurance.

text: Der deutsche Staat hat viele Aufgaben. Welche Aufgabe gehört dazu?
options: Er versorgt alle Einwohnerinnen und Einwohner kostenlos mit Zeitungen.

en.text: The German state has many tasks. Which one is among them?
options: It supplies all residents with newspapers free of charge.
en.context: Building roads and schools is a core task of the state. Producing cars or selling food is left to private business in a market economy.

text: Der deutsche Staat hat viele Aufgaben. Welche Aufgabe gehört nicht dazu?
options: Er bezahlt für alle Staatsangehörigen Urlaubsreisen.

en.text: The German state has many tasks. Which one is not among them?
options: It pays for holiday trips for all citizens.
en.context: The state pays child benefit and supports museums and athletes, but it does not pay for citizens' holidays. That is simply not a public task.

text: Welches Organ gehört nicht zu den Verfassungsorganen Deutschlands?

en.text: Which body is not one of Germany's constitutional bodies?
en.context: The citizens' assembly is not a constitutional body. The five are the Bundestag, the Bundesrat, the Federal President, the federal government and the Federal Constitutional Court.

text: Wer bestimmt in Deutschland die Schulpolitik?

en.text: Who determines school policy in Germany?
en.context: School policy is decided by the federal states, which is why curricula and school types differ from state to state. This is known as Kulturhoheit der Länder.

text: Die Wirtschaftsform in Deutschland nennt man …

en.text: The economic system in Germany is called …
en.context: Germany's system is called the social market economy: supply and demand set prices, while the state provides a social safety net and rules for fair competition.

text: Zu einem demokratischen Rechtsstaat gehört es nicht, dass …
options: Menschen sich kritisch über die Regierung äußern können.
Menschen von einer Privatpolizei ohne Grund verhaftet werden.
jemand ein Verbrechen begeht und deshalb verhaftet wird.

en.text: It is not part of a democratic state governed by the rule of law that …
options: people can speak critically about the government.
people are arrested by a private police force without reason.
someone commits a crime and is arrested for it.
en.context: Arrests without grounds by a private police force have no place in a state governed by the rule of law. Criticism, peaceful demonstrations and arrests following a crime are all perfectly normal.

text: Was bedeutet "Volkssouveränität"? Alle Staatsgewalt geht vom ...

en.text: What does "sovereignty of the people" mean? All state authority emanates from …
en.context: Article 20 says all state authority emanates from the people. Citizens exercise it through elections and votes, and through the organs of state they elect.

text: Was bedeutet "Rechtsstaat" in Deutschland?
options: Die Bürgerinnen und Bürger entscheiden über Gesetze.
Der Staat muss die Gesetze einhalten.

en.text: What does "state governed by the rule of law" mean in Germany?
options: The state must obey the law.
en.context: Rechtsstaat means the state itself is bound by the law. It has nothing to do with right-wing politics — "Recht" here means law, not the political right.

text: Was ist keine staatliche Gewalt in Deutschland?

en.text: What is not a branch of state power in Germany?
en.context: There is no such branch as a "Direktive". The three branches of state power are the legislature, the executive and the judiciary.

text: Was zeigt dieses Bild?

en.text: What does this picture show?
options: the seat of the Bundestag in Berlin
the Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe
en.context: The picture shows the Reichstag building in Berlin, the seat of the Bundestag since 1999. Its glass dome, open to visitors, has become a symbol of transparent government.

text: Welches Amt gehört in Deutschland zur Gemeindeverwaltung?

en.text: Which office belongs to municipal administration in Germany?
en.context: The Ordnungsamt, or public order office, is part of municipal administration. The tax office belongs to the state and the Federal Foreign Office to the federation.

text: Wer wird meistens zur Präsidentin/zum Präsidenten des Deutschen Bundestages gewählt?
options: die Ministerpräsidentin/der Ministerpräsident des größten Bundeslandes
eine Abgeordnete/ein Abgeordneter der stärksten Fraktion

en.text: Who is usually elected President of the German Bundestag?
options: the Minister-President of the largest federal state
a member of the largest parliamentary group
en.context: By long-standing convention the President of the Bundestag comes from the largest parliamentary group. The office ranks second in protocol after the Federal President.

text: Wer ernennt in Deutschland die Ministerinnen/die Minister der Bundesregierung?

en.text: Who appoints the ministers of the federal government in Germany?
options: the President of the Federal Constitutional Court
en.context: Federal ministers are formally appointed by the Federal President, on the proposal of the Chancellor. The Chancellor chooses them; the President signs the appointment.

text: Vor wie vielen Jahren gab es erstmals eine jüdische Gemeinde auf dem Gebiet des heutigen Deutschlands?

en.text: How many years ago was there first a Jewish community in the territory of present-day Germany?
en.context: A decree of Emperor Constantine from the year 321 mentions a Jewish community in Cologne, so Jewish life on German soil is around 1,700 years old.

text: In Deutschland gehören der Bundestag und der Bundesrat zur …

en.text: In Germany, the Bundestag and the Bundesrat belong to the …
en.context: The Bundestag and the Bundesrat both take part in making laws, so both belong to the legislature. The judiciary is the courts, the executive the government and administration.

text: Was bedeutet "Volkssouveränität"?
options: Die Königin/der König herrscht über das Volk.
Das Bundesverfassungsgericht steht über der Verfassung.
Die Interessenverbände üben die Souveränität zusammen mit der Regierung aus.
Die Staatsgewalt geht vom Volke aus.

en.text: What does "sovereignty of the people" mean?
options: The king or queen rules over the people.
The Federal Constitutional Court stands above the constitution.
Interest groups exercise sovereignty together with the government.
State authority emanates from the people.
en.context: Sovereignty of the people means state authority emanates from the people. It is the answer to the old idea that power belongs to a monarch by birth.

text: Wenn das Parlament eines deutschen Bundeslandes gewählt wird, nennt man das …

en.text: When the parliament of a German federal state is elected, this is called a …
en.context: Electing the parliament of a federal state is a Landtagswahl. Local elections choose municipal councils; the Bundestag election chooses the federal parliament.

text: Was gehört in Deutschland nicht zur Exekutive?

en.text: What is not part of the executive in Germany?
en.context: The courts are the judiciary, not the executive. The executive is the government together with the administration that carries out the law, such as the police and the tax office.

text: Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland ist heute gegliedert in …

en.text: The Federal Republic of Germany today is divided into …
options: an eastern state and a western state.
en.context: Germany is organised in three tiers: the federation, the states and the municipalities. The four occupation zones and the division into two states are long gone.

text: Es gehört nicht zu den Aufgaben des Deutschen Bundestages, …

en.text: It is not one of the tasks of the German Bundestag to …
en.context: Forming the cabinet is the Chancellor's job, not the Bundestag's. The Bundestag drafts and passes laws, scrutinises the government and elects the Chancellor.

text: Welche Städte haben die größten jüdischen Gemeinden in Deutschland?

en.text: Which cities have the largest Jewish communities in Germany?
en.context: Berlin and Munich have the largest Jewish communities in Germany today. Worms and Speyer were great medieval centres, but their communities are small now.

text: Was ist in Deutschland vor allem eine Aufgabe der Bundesländer?

en.text: What is above all a task of the federal states in Germany?
en.context: School policy is above all a matter for the federal states. Defence, foreign affairs and the main lines of economic policy belong to the federation.

text: Warum kontrolliert der Staat in Deutschland das Schulwesen?
options: weil es in Deutschland nur staatliche Schulen gibt
weil alle Schülerinnen und Schüler einen Schulabschluss haben müssen
weil es in den Bundesländern verschiedene Schulen gibt
weil es nach dem Grundgesetz seine Aufgabe ist

en.text: Why does the state supervise the school system in Germany?
options: because there are only state schools in Germany
because all pupils must have a school-leaving qualification
because there are different schools in the federal states
because under the Basic Law it is its task
en.context: Article 7 of the Basic Law places the entire school system under state supervision. That is why the state sets standards even for private schools.

text: Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland hat einen dreistufigen Verwaltungsaufbau. Wie heißt die unterste politische Stufe?

en.text: The Federal Republic of Germany has a three-tier administrative structure. What is the lowest political tier called?
en.context: The lowest tier is the municipality, the Gemeinde. Above it come the federal state and then the federation.

text: Der deutsche Bundespräsident Gustav Heinemann gibt Helmut Schmidt 1974 die Ernennungsurkunde zum deutschen Bundeskanzler. Was gehört zu den Aufgaben der deutschen Bundespräsidentin/des deutschen Bundespräsidenten?
options: Sie/Er schlägt die Kanzlerin/den Kanzler zur Wahl vor.

en.text: German Federal President Gustav Heinemann hands Helmut Schmidt the certificate of appointment as German Federal Chancellor in 1974. What is one of the tasks of the German Federal President?
options: They conduct the business of government.
They propose the Chancellor for election.
en.context: The Federal President proposes a candidate for Chancellor to the Bundestag and then appoints the person elected, as in the photo. Running the government is the Chancellor's job, not the President's.

text: Wo hält sich die deutsche Bundeskanzlerin/der deutsche Bundeskanzler am häufigsten auf? Am häufigsten ist sie/er …
options: in Bonn, weil sich dort das Bundeskanzleramt und der Bundestag befinden.
auf Schloss Meseberg, dem Gästehaus der Bundesregierung, um Staatsgäste zu empfangen.
auf Schloss Bellevue, dem Amtssitz der Bundespräsidentin/des Bundespräsidenten, um Staatsgäste zu empfangen.
in Berlin, weil sich dort das Bundeskanzleramt und der Bundestag befinden.

en.text: Where does the German Federal Chancellor spend most time? Most often they are …
options: in Bonn, because the Federal Chancellery and the Bundestag are there.
at Meseberg Palace, the federal government's guest house, to receive state guests.
at Bellevue Palace, the official residence of the Federal President, to receive state guests.
in Berlin, because the Federal Chancellery and the Bundestag are there.
en.context: The Chancellor spends most time in Berlin, where both the Federal Chancellery and the Bundestag are. Meseberg and Bellevue are used only occasionally, and Bellevue is the President's residence.

text: Wie heißt die jetzige Bundeskanzlerin/der jetzige Bundeskanzler von Deutschland?

en.text: What is the name of Germany's current Federal Chancellor?
en.context: Friedrich Merz has been Federal Chancellor since 2025. He is the tenth person to hold the office since 1949.

text: Die beiden größten Fraktionen im Deutschen Bundestag heißen zurzeit …

en.text: The two largest parliamentary groups in the German Bundestag are currently …
en.context: After the 2025 federal election the two largest groups in the Bundestag are the CDU/CSU and the AfD. The largest group normally provides the President of the Bundestag.

text: Wie heißt das Parlament für ganz Deutschland?

en.text: What is the parliament for the whole of Germany called?
en.context: The parliament for the whole of Germany is the Bundestag. The Volkskammer was the GDR's parliament and no longer exists.

text: Wie heißt Deutschlands heutiges Staatsoberhaupt?

en.text: What is the name of Germany's current head of state?
en.context: Frank-Walter Steinmeier has been Federal President, and thus head of state, since 2017. He was re-elected for a second term in 2022.

text: Was bedeutet die Abkürzung CDU in Deutschland?

en.text: What does the abbreviation CDU stand for in Germany?
options: Club Deutscher Unternehmer (Club of German Entrepreneurs)
Christlicher Deutscher Umweltschutz (Christian German Environmental Protection)
en.context: CDU stands for Christlich Demokratische Union, the Christian Democratic Union. It has been one of the two big parties since 1949.

text: Was ist die Bundeswehr?

en.text: What is the Bundeswehr?
en.context: The Bundeswehr is Germany's armed forces, founded in 1955. It is a parliamentary army: deployments abroad need the Bundestag's approval.

text: Was bedeutet die Abkürzung SPD?

en.text: What does the abbreviation SPD stand for?
options: Sozialistische Partei Deutschlands (Socialist Party of Germany)
Sozialpolitische Partei Deutschlands (Social Policy Party of Germany)
Sozialdemokratische Partei Deutschlands (Social Democratic Party of Germany)
Sozialgerechte Partei Deutschlands (Socially Just Party of Germany)
en.context: SPD stands for Sozialdemokratische Partei Deutschlands, the Social Democratic Party. Founded in 1863, it is Germany's oldest party.

text: Was bedeutet die Abkürzung FDP in Deutschland?

en.text: What does the abbreviation FDP stand for in Germany?
en.context: FDP stands for Freie Demokratische Partei, the Free Democratic Party, which stands in the liberal tradition.

text: Welches Gericht in Deutschland ist zuständig für die Auslegung des Grundgesetzes?

en.text: Which court in Germany is responsible for interpreting the Basic Law?
en.context: The Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe interprets the Basic Law. It can strike down laws and is the final authority on basic rights.

text: Wer wählt die Bundeskanzlerin/den Bundeskanzler in Deutschland?

en.text: Who elects the Federal Chancellor in Germany?
en.context: The Chancellor is elected by the Bundestag, on the Federal President's proposal. Voters choose the Bundestag, and the Bundestag chooses the Chancellor.

text: Wer leitet das deutsche Bundeskabinett?

en.text: Who chairs the German federal cabinet?
en.context: The Chancellor chairs the federal cabinet and sets the general policy guidelines — the Richtlinienkompetenz of Article 65.

text: Wer wählt die deutsche Bundeskanzlerin/den deutschen Bundeskanzler?

en.text: Who elects the German Federal Chancellor?
en.context: It is the Bundestag that elects the Chancellor. The Federal Convention has only one job: electing the Federal President.

text: Welche Hauptaufgabe hat die deutsche Bundespräsidentin/der deutsche Bundespräsident? Sie/Er …

en.text: What is the main task of the German Federal President? They …
en.context: The Federal President represents the country at home and abroad. The office is largely ceremonial, standing above day-to-day party politics.

text: Wer bildet den deutschen Bundesrat?
options: die Ministerinnen und Minister der Bundesregierung

en.text: Who makes up the German Bundesrat?
options: the ministers of the federal government
the government representatives of the federal states
en.context: The Bundesrat is made up of members of the state governments, not of elected delegates. Through it the states take part in federal legislation.

text: Wer wählt in Deutschland die Bundespräsidentin/den Bundespräsidenten?

en.text: Who elects the Federal President in Germany?
en.context: The Federal President is elected by the Federal Convention, which consists of all members of the Bundestag plus an equal number of delegates chosen by the state parliaments.

text: Wer ist das Staatsoberhaupt der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?

en.text: Who is the head of state of the Federal Republic of Germany?
en.context: The head of state is the Federal President. The Chancellor is head of government, which is a different role.

text: Die parlamentarische Opposition im Deutschen Bundestag …
options: schlägt die Regierungschefinnen/Regierungschefs der Länder vor.

en.text: The parliamentary opposition in the German Bundestag …
options: decides who becomes a federal minister.
determines who sits in the Bundesrat.
proposes the heads of government of the federal states.
en.context: The opposition's central task is to scrutinise the government, question its decisions and offer alternatives. Appointing ministers is not its business.

text: Wie nennt man in Deutschland die Vereinigung von Abgeordneten einer Partei im Parlament?

en.text: What is the association of members of one party in parliament called in Germany?
en.context: Members of one party in parliament form a Fraktion, a parliamentary group. Group status brings rights such as committee seats and speaking time.

text: Die deutschen Bundesländer wirken an der Gesetzgebung des Bundes mit durch …

en.text: The German federal states take part in federal legislation through …
en.context: The states take part in federal legislation through the Bundesrat. Many laws cannot come into force without its consent.

text: In Deutschland kann ein Regierungswechsel in einem Bundesland Auswirkungen auf die Bundespolitik haben. Das Regieren wird …
options: schwieriger, wenn sich dadurch die Mehrheit im Bundestag ändert.
leichter, wenn dadurch neue Parteien in den Bundesrat kommen.
schwieriger, wenn dadurch die Mehrheit im Bundesrat verändert wird.
leichter, wenn es sich um ein reiches Bundesland handelt.

en.text: In Germany, a change of government in a federal state can affect federal politics. Governing becomes …
options: more difficult if this changes the majority in the Bundestag.
easier if this brings new parties into the Bundesrat.
more difficult if this changes the majority in the Bundesrat.
easier if it is a wealthy federal state.
en.context: State governments send their representatives to the Bundesrat, so a change of government in one state can shift the majority there and make governing harder for the federal government.

text: Was bedeutet die Abkürzung CSU in Deutschland?

en.text: What does the abbreviation CSU stand for in Germany?
options: Christlich Süddeutsche Union (Christian South German Union)
Christlich Sozialer Unternehmerverband (Christian Social Employers' Association)
en.context: CSU stands for Christlich Soziale Union, the Christian Social Union. It stands only in Bavaria, where the CDU does not compete.

text: Je mehr "Zweitstimmen" eine Partei bei einer Bundestagswahl bekommt, desto …
options: mehr Direktkandidaten der Partei ziehen ins Parlament ein.
größer ist das Risiko, eine Koalition bilden zu müssen.
mehr Sitze erhält die Partei im Parlament.

en.text: The more "second votes" a party receives in a Bundestag election, the …
options: fewer first votes it can have.
more of the party's direct candidates enter parliament.
greater the risk of having to form a coalition.
more seats the party gets in parliament.
en.context: The second vote decides how many seats a party gets in the Bundestag, which makes it the more important of the two votes.

text: Ab welchem Alter darf man in Deutschland an der Wahl zum Deutschen Bundestag teilnehmen?

en.text: From what age may you take part in the election of the German Bundestag?
en.context: You may vote in Bundestag elections from the age of 18. Some states allow 16-year-olds to vote locally, but not federally.

text: Was gilt für die meisten Kinder in Deutschland?

en.text: What applies to most children in Germany?
en.context: School attendance is compulsory for most children in Germany, usually for nine or ten years. Voting is a right, not a duty.

text: Wie kann jemand, der den Holocaust leugnet, bestraft werden?
options: mit Freiheitsstrafe bis zu fünf Jahren oder mit Geldstrafe

en.text: How can someone who denies the Holocaust be punished?
options: up to 100 hours of community service
not at all, Holocaust denial is permitted
with a prison sentence of up to five years or a fine
en.context: Denying the Holocaust is a criminal offence under section 130 of the Criminal Code, punishable by up to five years in prison or a fine.

text: Was bezahlt man in Deutschland automatisch, wenn man fest angestellt ist?

en.text: What do you pay automatically in Germany if you are in permanent employment?
en.context: Anyone in permanent employment automatically pays social insurance contributions, deducted from wages along with income tax.

text: Wenn Abgeordnete im Deutschen Bundestag ihre Fraktion wechseln, …
options: dürfen sie nicht mehr an den Sitzungen des Parlaments teilnehmen.
kann die Regierung ihre Mehrheit verlieren.
muss die Bundespräsidentin/der Bundespräsident zuvor ihr/sein Einverständnis geben.
dürfen die Wählerinnen/Wähler dieser Abgeordneten noch einmal wählen.

en.text: If members of the German Bundestag change their parliamentary group, …
options: they may no longer take part in sittings of parliament.
the government can lose its majority.
the Federal President must give their consent beforehand.
the voters of those members may vote again.
en.context: Members keep their seats if they switch groups, so the government can lose its majority. Members are bound only by their conscience, not by party instructions.

text: Wer bezahlt in Deutschland die Sozialversicherungen?

en.text: Who pays for social insurance in Germany?
en.context: Social insurance is paid jointly by employers and employees, who each carry roughly half the contributions.

text: Was gehört nicht zur gesetzlichen Sozialversicherung?

en.text: What is not part of statutory social insurance?
en.context: Life insurance is private cover, not part of statutory social insurance. The statutory branches are health, pension, unemployment, long-term care and accident insurance.

text: Gewerkschaften sind Interessenverbände der …

en.text: Trade unions are interest groups representing …
en.context: Trade unions represent employees. Employers have their own organisations, and the two sides negotiate collective agreements with each other.

text: Womit kann man in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland geehrt werden, wenn man auf politischem, wirtschaftlichem, kulturellem, geistigem oder sozialem Gebiet eine besondere Leistung erbracht hat? Mit dem …

en.text: What can you be honoured with in the Federal Republic of Germany for outstanding achievement in political, economic, cultural, intellectual or social life? With the …
options: honorary title "Hero of the German Democratic Republic"
en.context: The Bundesverdienstkreuz, the Federal Cross of Merit, is the highest general honour the Federal Republic awards. It is given for outstanding service to the country.

text: Was wird in Deutschland als "Ampelkoalition" bezeichnet? Die Zusammenarbeit …
options: der Bundestagsfraktionen von CDU und CSU
von SPD, FDP und Bündnis 90/Die Grünen in einer Regierung
von CSU, Die LINKE und Bündnis 90/Die Grünen in einer Regierung
der Bundestagsfraktionen von CDU und SPD

en.text: What is referred to in Germany as a "traffic light coalition"? The cooperation …
options: of the Bundestag groups of the CDU and the CSU
of the SPD, the FDP and Bündnis 90/Die Grünen in a government
of the CSU, Die LINKE and Bündnis 90/Die Grünen in a government
of the Bundestag groups of the CDU and the SPD
en.context: A "traffic light" coalition is one of SPD (red), FDP (yellow) and the Greens — the colours of a traffic light. Germany had such a government from 2021 to 2024.

text: Eine Frau in Deutschland verliert ihre Arbeit. Was darf nicht der Grund für diese Entlassung sein?
options: Die Frau ist lange krank und arbeitsunfähig.
Die Frau kam oft zu spät zur Arbeit.
Die Frau erledigt private Sachen während der Arbeitszeit.
Die Frau bekommt ein Kind und ihr Chef weiß das.

en.text: A woman in Germany loses her job. What may not be the reason for this dismissal?
options: The woman has been ill and unable to work for a long time.
The woman was often late for work.
The woman deals with private matters during working hours.
The woman is having a baby and her boss knows this.
en.context: Dismissing a woman because she is pregnant is forbidden by the Maternity Protection Act. Poor timekeeping or private business in work time can be legitimate grounds.

text: Was ist eine Aufgabe von Wahlhelferinnen/Wahlhelfern in Deutschland?
options: Sie helfen alten Menschen bei der Stimmabgabe in der Wahlkabine.
Sie schreiben die Wahlbenachrichtigungen vor der Wahl.
Sie geben Zwischenergebnisse an die Medien weiter.
Sie zählen die Stimmen nach dem Ende der Wahl.

en.text: What is one task of election helpers in Germany?
options: They help elderly people cast their vote in the polling booth.
They write the polling cards before the election.
They pass interim results on to the media.
They count the votes after the election closes.
en.context: Election helpers count the votes once polling closes. They must not influence voters or leak interim results.

text: In Deutschland helfen ehrenamtliche Wahlhelferinnen und Wahlhelfer bei den Wahlen. Was ist eine Aufgabe von Wahlhelferinnen/Wahlhelfern?
options: Sie helfen Kindern und alten Menschen beim Wählen.
Sie schreiben Karten und Briefe mit der Angabe des Wahllokals.
Sie geben Zwischenergebnisse an Journalisten weiter.
Sie zählen die Stimmen nach dem Ende der Wahl.

en.text: In Germany, volunteer election helpers assist with elections. What is one task of election helpers?
options: They help children and elderly people to vote.
They write cards and letters stating the polling station.
They pass interim results on to journalists.
They count the votes after the election closes.
en.context: Volunteer election helpers run the polling station and count the votes afterwards. Their work is what makes the count public and verifiable.

text: Für wie viele Jahre wird der Bundestag in Deutschland gewählt?

en.text: For how many years is the Bundestag elected in Germany?
en.context: The Bundestag is elected for four years. An early election is possible but rare.

text: Bei einer Bundestagswahl in Deutschland darf jede/jeder wählen, die/der …
options: in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland wohnt und wählen möchte.
Bürgerin/Bürger der Bundesrepublik Deutschland ist und mindestens 18 Jahre alt ist.
seit mindestens 3 Jahren in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland lebt.
Bürgerin/Bürger der Bundesrepublik Deutschland ist und mindestens 21 Jahre alt ist.

en.text: In a Bundestag election in Germany, anyone may vote who …
options: lives in the Federal Republic of Germany and wants to vote.
is a citizen of the Federal Republic of Germany and is at least 18 years old.
has lived in the Federal Republic of Germany for at least 3 years.
is a citizen of the Federal Republic of Germany and is at least 21 years old.
en.context: You may vote in a Bundestag election if you are a German citizen and at least 18 years old. Residence alone is not enough.

text: Wie oft gibt es normalerweise Bundestagswahlen in Deutschland?

en.text: How often are Bundestag elections normally held in Germany?
en.context: Bundestag elections are normally held every four years, matching the parliament's term.

text: Für wie viele Jahre wird der Bundestag in Deutschland gewählt?

en.text: For how many years is the Bundestag elected in Germany?
en.context: The Bundestag's term is four years, after which it must face the voters again.

text: Welche Handlungen mit Bezug auf den Staat Israel sind in Deutschland verboten?
options: das Aufhängen einer israelischen Flagge auf dem Privatgrundstück
eine Diskussion über die Politik Israels
der öffentliche Aufruf zur Vernichtung Israels

en.text: Which actions relating to the State of Israel are prohibited in Germany?
options: flying an Israeli flag on private property
publicly calling for the destruction of Israel
en.context: Publicly calling for the destruction of Israel is a criminal offence in Germany. Criticising Israeli government policy, by contrast, is covered by freedom of expression.

text: Die Wahlen in Deutschland sind …

en.text: Elections in Germany are …
en.context: Elections in Germany are secret: nobody may find out how you voted. That is why polling booths and sealed ballot boxes exist.

text: Wahlen in Deutschland gewinnt die Partei, die …
options: die meisten Männer mehrheitlich gewählt haben.
die meisten Stimmen bei den Arbeiterinnen/Arbeitern bekommen hat.
die meisten Erststimmen für ihre Kanzlerkandidatin/ihren Kanzlerkandidaten erhalten hat.

en.text: Elections in Germany are won by the party that …
options: the majority of men voted for.
received the most votes among workers.
received the most first votes for its candidate for Chancellor.
en.context: The party with the most votes wins the election. Every vote counts the same, regardless of the voter's sex or occupation.

text: An demokratischen Wahlen in Deutschland teilzunehmen ist …

en.text: Taking part in democratic elections in Germany is …
en.context: Voting is a right, not a duty. There is no compulsory voting in Germany, and nobody may be penalised for staying at home.

text: Was bedeutet "aktives Wahlrecht" in Deutschland?
options: Man muss zur Auszählung der Stimmen gehen.

en.text: What does "active right to vote" mean in Germany?
options: You have to go and vote.
You have to attend the counting of the votes.
en.context: The active right to vote is the right to cast a vote. The right to stand for election is the passive right to vote.

text: Wenn Sie bei einer Bundestagswahl in Deutschland wählen dürfen, heißt das …

en.text: If you are allowed to vote in a Bundestag election in Germany, this is called …
en.context: Being allowed to vote is the active right to vote, which you have as a German citizen from the age of 18.

text: Wie viel Prozent der Zweitstimmen müssen Parteien mindestens bekommen, um in den Deutschen Bundestag gewählt zu werden?

en.text: What is the minimum percentage of second votes a party must receive to be elected to the German Bundestag?
en.context: A party needs at least 5% of the second votes to enter the Bundestag, unless it wins enough constituency seats directly.

text: Wer darf bei den rund 40 jüdischen Makkabi-Sportvereinen Mitglied werden?

en.text: Who may become a member of the roughly 40 Jewish Maccabi sports clubs?
en.context: The Maccabi sports clubs are Jewish in tradition but open to everyone, whatever their religion or nationality.

text: Wahlen in Deutschland sind frei. Was bedeutet das?
options: Alle verurteilten Straftäterinnen/Straftäter dürfen nicht wählen.
Wenn ich wählen gehen möchte, muss meine Arbeitgeberin/mein Arbeitgeber mir frei geben.
Jede Person kann ohne Zwang entscheiden, ob sie wählen möchte und wen sie wählen möchte.
Ich kann frei entscheiden, wo ich wählen gehen möchte.

en.text: Elections in Germany are free. What does that mean?
options: All convicted offenders are not allowed to vote.
If I want to go and vote, my employer must give me time off.
Every person can decide without coercion whether they want to vote and whom they want to vote for.
I can freely decide where I want to go and vote.
en.context: Free elections mean each person decides without coercion whether to vote at all and whom to vote for.

text: Das Wahlsystem in Deutschland ist ein …

en.text: The electoral system in Germany is …
options: a majority and proportional representation system.
en.context: Germany combines both systems: constituency seats are decided by simple majority, while the overall distribution of seats follows proportional representation.

text: Eine Partei möchte in den Deutschen Bundestag. Sie muss aber einen Mindestanteil an Wählerstimmen haben. Das heißt …

en.text: A party wants to enter the German Bundestag. But it must have a minimum share of the votes. This is called …
en.context: The minimum share of votes needed is called the 5% threshold, the Fünfprozenthürde. It is meant to keep parliament workable.

text: Welchem Grundsatz unterliegen Wahlen in Deutschland? Wahlen in Deutschland sind …

en.text: Which principles govern elections in Germany? Elections in Germany are …
en.context: The 5% threshold is the minimum share of the votes a party must reach to enter parliament.

text: Was ist in Deutschland die "5%-Hürde"?
options: Abstimmungsregelung im Bundestag für kleine Parteien
Mindestanteil an Wählerstimmen, um ins Parlament zu kommen

en.text: What is the "5% threshold" in Germany?
options: a voting rule in the Bundestag for small parties
an attendance check in the Bundestag for votes
the minimum share of votes needed to enter parliament
an attendance check in the Bundesrat for votes
en.context: The 5% threshold is not a rule about voting inside parliament — it decides who gets into parliament in the first place.

text: Die Bundestagswahl in Deutschland ist die Wahl …

en.text: The Bundestag election in Germany is the election of …
options: the parliaments of the federal states.
en.context: The Bundestag election elects the parliament for Germany. The Chancellor is then chosen by that parliament, not directly by voters.

text: In einer Demokratie ist eine Funktion von regelmäßigen Wahlen, …
options: die Bürgerinnen und Bürger zu zwingen, ihre Stimme abzugeben.
nach dem Willen der Wählermehrheit den Wechsel der Regierung zu ermöglichen.
den Armen mehr Macht zu geben.

en.text: In a democracy, one function of regular elections is …
options: to force citizens to cast their vote.
to make a change of government possible according to the will of the majority of voters.
to keep the country's existing laws in place.
to give more power to the poor.
en.context: Regular elections let the majority change the government peacefully. That possibility of a change of power is the heart of democracy.

text: Was bekommen wahlberechtigte Bürgerinnen und Bürger in Deutschland vor einer Wahl?
options: eine Wahlerlaubnis von der Bundespräsidentin/von dem Bundespräsidenten

en.text: What do citizens entitled to vote receive in Germany before an election?
options: a polling card from the municipality
permission to vote from the Federal President
a notification from the Federal Convention
a notification from the parish office
en.context: Before an election, voters receive a polling card from their municipality telling them where and when to vote.

text: Warum gibt es die 5%-Hürde im Wahlgesetz der Bundesrepublik Deutschland? Es gibt sie, weil …
options: die Programme von vielen kleinen Parteien viele Gemeinsamkeiten haben.
die Bürgerinnen und Bürger bei vielen kleinen Parteien die Orientierung verlieren können.
viele kleine Parteien die Regierungsbildung erschweren.
die kleinen Parteien nicht so viel Geld haben, um die Politikerinnen und Politiker zu bezahlen.

en.text: Why is there a 5% threshold in the electoral law of the Federal Republic of Germany? It exists because …
options: the programmes of many small parties have a lot in common.
citizens can lose their bearings when there are many small parties.
many small parties make forming a government more difficult.
the small parties do not have enough money to pay the politicians.
en.context: The threshold exists because a parliament split among many small parties makes forming a stable government difficult. The Weimar Republic's experience is the historical reason.

text: Parlamentsmitglieder, die von den Bürgerinnen und Bürgern gewählt werden, nennt man …

en.text: Members of parliament elected by the citizens are called …
en.context: Members of parliament elected by citizens are called Abgeordnete, deputies. They represent the whole people, not just their own voters.

text: Vom Volk gewählt wird in Deutschland …

en.text: In Germany, the body elected by the people is …
options: the Minister-President of a federal state.
en.context: Of these, only the Bundestag is elected directly by the people. The Chancellor, the President and the state premiers are all elected by other bodies.

text: Welcher Stimmzettel wäre bei einer Bundestagswahl gültig? In Anlehnung an Bundeswahlordnung (BWO), Anlage 26

en.text: Which ballot paper would be valid in a Bundestag election? Based on the Federal Electoral Regulations (BWO), Annex 26
en.context: A valid ballot has exactly one cross in each column — one first vote and one second vote. More than one mark in a column makes that vote invalid.

text: In Deutschland ist eine Bürgermeisterin/ein Bürgermeister …

en.text: In Germany, a mayor is …
en.context: A Bürgermeister is the head of a municipality. In most states the post is filled by direct election.

text: Viele Menschen in Deutschland arbeiten in ihrer Freizeit ehrenamtlich. Was bedeutet das?
options: Sie arbeiten freiwillig und unbezahlt in Vereinen und Verbänden.
Sie arbeiten in einem Krankenhaus und verdienen dabei Geld.

en.text: Many people in Germany do voluntary work in their free time. What does that mean?
options: They work voluntarily and unpaid in clubs and associations.
They work in the federal government.
They work in a hospital and earn money doing so.
en.context: Voluntary work, Ehrenamt, means giving your time unpaid to clubs, associations and charities. Millions of people in Germany do it.

text: Was ist bei Bundestags- und Landtagswahlen in Deutschland erlaubt?
options: Der Ehemann wählt für seine Frau mit.
Man kann durch Briefwahl seine Stimme abgeben.
Man kann am Wahltag telefonisch seine Stimme abgeben.
Kinder ab dem Alter von 14 Jahren dürfen wählen.

en.text: What is permitted in Bundestag and state parliament elections in Germany?
options: A husband also votes for his wife.
You can cast your vote by postal ballot.
You can cast your vote by telephone on election day.
Children aged 14 and over may vote.
en.context: Postal voting is allowed in Bundestag and state elections and needs no special reason. Voting by phone, or on someone else's behalf, is not permitted.

text: Man will die Buslinie abschaffen, mit der Sie immer zur Arbeit fahren. Was können Sie machen, um die Buslinie zu erhalten?
options: Ich beteilige mich an einer Bürgerinitiative für die Erhaltung der Buslinie oder gründe selber eine Initiative.
Ich werde Mitglied in einem Sportverein und trainiere Radfahren.
Ich wende mich an das Finanzamt, weil ich als Steuerzahlerin/Steuerzahler ein Recht auf die Buslinie habe.
Ich schreibe einen Brief an das Forstamt der Gemeinde.

en.text: There are plans to scrap the bus route you always take to work. What can you do to keep the bus route?
options: I take part in a citizens' initiative to keep the bus route, or start an initiative myself.
I join a sports club and train for cycling.
I contact the tax office, because as a taxpayer I have a right to the bus route.
I write a letter to the municipal forestry office.
en.context: Starting or joining a citizens' initiative is the normal way to press for a local decision to be changed. It is an everyday use of the freedom of assembly.

text: Wen vertreten die Gewerkschaften in Deutschland?

en.text: Whom do the trade unions represent in Germany?
en.context: Trade unions represent employees in dealings with employers, above all in negotiating pay and working conditions.

text: Sie gehen in Deutschland zum Arbeitsgericht bei …
options: ungerechtfertigter Kündigung durch Ihre Chefin/Ihren Chef.

en.text: In Germany you go to the labour court in the case of …
en.context: The labour court handles disputes between employees and employers, including unfair dismissal. Neighbours and traffic accidents belong elsewhere.

text: Welches Gericht ist in Deutschland bei Konflikten in der Arbeitswelt zuständig?

en.text: Which court is responsible for conflicts in working life in Germany?
en.context: Conflicts in working life go to the Arbeitsgericht, the labour court. The first instance is free of court fees.

text: Was kann ich in Deutschland machen, wenn mir meine Arbeitgeberin/mein Arbeitgeber zu Unrecht gekündigt hat?
options: weiterarbeiten und freundlich zur Chefin/zum Chef sein
ein Mahnverfahren gegen die Arbeitgeberin/den Arbeitgeber führen
die Arbeitgeberin/den Arbeitgeber bei der Polizei anzeigen

en.text: What can I do in Germany if my employer has dismissed me unlawfully?
options: keep working and be friendly to the boss
bring debt recovery proceedings against the employer
file an action for unfair dismissal
report the employer to the police
en.context: You can bring an action for unfair dismissal, a Kündigungsschutzklage. It must be filed within three weeks of receiving the notice.

text: Wann kommt es in Deutschland zu einem Prozess vor Gericht? Wenn jemand …
options: eine Straftat begangen hat und angeklagt wird.
eine andere Meinung als die der Regierung vertritt.
sein Auto falsch geparkt hat und es abgeschleppt wird.

en.text: When does a court trial take place in Germany? When someone …
options: has committed a criminal offence and is charged.
holds a different opinion from the government's.
has parked their car wrongly and it is towed away.
en.context: A criminal trial follows when someone is charged with an offence. Changing religion or having a car towed does not lead to a trial.

text: Was macht eine Schöffin/ein Schöffe in Deutschland? Sie/Er …
options: entscheidet mit Richterinnen/Richtern über Schuld und Strafe.

en.text: What does a lay judge do in Germany? They …
